glosses: (nur) am Tag wach und nachtsüber ruhend

examples.text: „Doch am meisten macht es Spaß, die Kinder morgens aus dem Schlaf zu wecken, da ich tagaktiv bin.“

translations.source_sense_description: Zoologie: (nur) am Tag wach und nachtsüber ruhend

glosses: Happening or occurring during daylight, or primarily active during that time.

examples.text: However, in general, lizards are more diurnal than rattlers, which may be one of the reasons why young rattlers are more diurnal than adults.
Ere twice the horses of the sun shall bring / Their fiery torcher his diurnal ring.

glosses: Said of a flower that is open, or releasing its perfume during daylight hours, but not at night.
Having a daily cycle that is completed every 24 hours, usually referring to tasks, processes, tides, or sunrise to sunset; circadian.
Done once every day; daily, quotidian.
A flower that opens only in the day.
A book containing canonical offices performed during the day, hence not matins.

examples.text: He was by birth, some authors write, / A Russian, some a Muscovite, / And 'mong the Cossacks had been bred, / Of whom we in diurnals read.

translations.source_sense_description: Zoologie: (nur) am Tag wach und nachtsüber ruhend

examples.text: Mouvement diurne. Mouvement apparent, accompli, en vingt-quatre heures, par les étoiles autour de la Terre.
Le mouvement diurne de la Terre, sa rotation autour de son axe.

glosses: Par opposition à nocturne. Qui a lieu, qui se manifeste pendant les heures où le Soleil éclaire la Terre.

examples.text: La tomate exige une photopériode diurne très grande. Selon Bendix et Went, la croissance augmente linéairement en fonction de la photopériode entre 4 et 20 heures de jour.

glosses: Dont la période d'activité se situe entre le lever et le coucher du Soleil.

examples.text: Les Lépidoptères diurnes ou, comme nom, les diurnes.

glosses: Dont les accès se produisent pendant la journée.
Actes diurnes : Synonyme dactes diurnaux. Voir l'adjectif diurnal.

examples.text: Les actes diurnes chez les Romains.
